span.p:
recording
may we record your voice?

div.style: color: rgb(11, 37, 69) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

color: rgb(74, 47, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
NO intake. The call proceeds anyway.
Brief stays context-only - and is still
correctly routed, because the menu did that.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
why health is its own scope. Health information
is a special category under PDPA. Bundling it into
a single yes/no would be the easy build and the
wrong one - a motor claim caller should not have to
consent to health processing to report a dent.

div.style: color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
every consent recorded with
scope - granted - when - basis - channel

div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
retention and erasure (P7)
recordings expire on a clock. Erasure has to reach
the blob store, the transcript, the brief versions
AND the event log - which is why blob refs are
indirect rather than inlined everywhere.
